references.text: God gives Abraham a similar promise to make him into a great nation and bless him.
God promises to make Abraham's descendants as numerous as the dust of the earth, so that they cannot be counted.
God promises to make Abraham's descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky.
God makes a covenant with Abraham, which is directly parallel to the covenant established in 17:2.
The immediate elaboration of the covenant: Abraham shall become the father of many nations and be exceedingly fruitful.
God renews his promise to make Abraham's descendants as numerous as the stars and the sand by the sea.
Paul refers to Abraham's faith and God's promise to bless all nations through him.
Lev 26:9 confirms that the promise of multitude and covenant given to Abraham (Gen 17:2) is valid for the nation of Israel.
Heb 6:14 quotes God's oath to make Abraham numerous (as in Gen 17:2) to confirm God's infinite faithfulness.
Ezek 16:60 shows that the covenant established in Gen 17:2 is eternal and restored by God's grace even after breach.
Ezek 16:62 confirms that God's promise to establish a covenant in Gen 17:2 is an eternal act that will be fulfilled in the future.
Gen 9:9 establishes God's eternal covenant with all humanity, which serves as the universal framework for the special covenant with Abraham in Gen 17:2.
Gen 48:4 confirms and repeats the promise of multitude and land given to Abraham in Gen 17:2, now directed toward Joseph.
Num 14:12 confirms that the promise to make Abraham's offspring numerous (Gen 17:2) is maintained even after breach.
Exod 32:10 shows that the promise to make Abraham into a great nation (Gen 17:2) stands independent of Israel's breach.
Gen 17:11 defines circumcision as the sign of the covenant established in Gen 17:2.
Ezek 37:26 confirms that the promise to make the people numerous and establish an everlasting covenant (Gen 17:2) will be fulfilled in the future.
Ps 89:29 shows that David's covenant is an extension of the everlasting covenant established with Abraham in Gen 17:2.
Gen 12:2 is the first retelling of the promise that is confirmed and expanded upon in Gen 17:2.
Gen 6:18 establishes God's covenant strategy with Noah, which serves as a precursor to the special covenant with Abraham in Gen 17:2.
Gen 32:13 confirms that the promise to make Abraham's descendants numerous (Gen 17:2) is a valid basis for prayer.
Zech 2:15 shows that the promise that Abraham will become a multitude of nations (Gen 17:2) will be fulfilled through all peoples.
Acts 3:25 confirms that the covenant established with Abraham in Gen 17:2 is the foundation for salvation for all nations.
Luke 1:73 confirms that God's oath to Abraham (Gen 17:2) is fulfilled in Jesus' birth.
Acts 7:17 describes the historical fulfillment of the promise to make Abraham's descendants numerous (Gen 17:2) in Egypt.
